statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5318(g)?
statutory.answer: No. 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) suspicious activity reporting requirements are not triggered on these facts alone.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) authorizes/mandates “suspicious activity reporting requirements” for “financial institutions” to report suspicious transactions to the government (per implementing regulations) and provides related protections (e.g., confidentiality/safe harbor). The fact pattern describes a business customer (SYN_efad9649) and a list of wires/ACH transfers, but it does not identify any covered “financial institution” subject to § 5318(g), nor does it state that a financial institution detected suspicious activity, had a reporting obligation under the applicable SAR rules, or failed to file a SAR. While the transactions are large, the facts do not establish the statutory elements needed to apply § 5318(g) (covered reporter + suspicious transaction determination + reporting/filing context). Therefore, § 5318(g) suspicious activity reporting requirements cannot be determined to apply from the provided facts.
